### App for "teaching" sample size
### André Moser, Sep 2026


library(shiny)
library(tidyverse)
library(waiter)
library(Hmisc)

ui <- fluidPage(
  titlePanel("Sample size calculation App"),
  p(
    "This App helps you plan the sample size for a two-arm superiority clinical trial under different effect size scenarios.",
    tags$span(
      "There are three tabs, one for each type of outcome: binary, continuous, and ordinal.",
      style = "color: red;"
    )
  ),
  br(),
  tabsetPanel(
    tabPanel(
      "Binary outcome",
      br(),
      p("This tab performs a sample size calculation for a binary endpoint, expressing the effect to detect as either a risk difference or an odds ratio versus the proportion in the control arm"),
      div(
        style = "border: 1px solid #ccc; border-radius: 5px; padding: 10px 15px; margin-bottom: 15px;",
        tags$strong("Case scenario 1: The ESCAPE trial in 2015 investigated rapid endovascular thrombectomy vs standard of care at that time in patients with acute anterior-circulation large-vessel ischemic stroke"),
        tags$a("[https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1414905]", href="https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1414905"),
        tags$strong(". We use the results of the ESCAPE trial to plan a new trial and assume that this is the best available evidence for this clinical trial setting."),
        tags$ul(
          tags$li("T1: The authors of the ESCAPE trial reported a proportion of patients with a modified Rankin score 0 to 2 of 29% in the control group and 53% in the intervention group.  What is the required sample size for a power of 0.8? Set alpha=0.05 and use a two-sided testing scenario. Hint: Set the 'minimum and maximum risk difference to detect' to the same value so that it matches the required inputs."),
          tags$li("T2: Write down the corresponding odds ratio from the Table output."),
          tags$li("T3: Investigate 'Plot 1'. What do the gray and blue curves indicate? What do the red and blue area indicate? What are the values of these areas?"),
          tags$li("T4: Change the test direction to the one-sided test direction 'intervention is greater than control'. What happens to the sample size? Why?"),
          tags$li("T5: Which alpha level is needed so that you have the same sample size as in the two-sided scenario? Set this level accordingly."),
          tags$li("T6: Decrease the power to 0.5. What is the value of the blue area? Why is the sample size decreasing?"),
          tags$li("T7: Increase the 'Maximum difference to detect' to 0.54. Observe the changing sample size across the different risk difference scenarios. Why do you need less patients?"),
          tags$li("Continue with the tasks in the 'Continuous outcome' tab above."),
        )
      ),
      sidebarLayout(
        sidebarPanel(
          numericInput(
            inputId = "nominal_alpha",
            label   = "alpha:",
            value   = 0.05,
            min     = 0,
            max     = 1
          ),
          numericInput(
            inputId = "p_0",
            label   = "Proportion in control arm",
            value   = 0.5,
            min     = 0,
            max     = 1
          ),
          sliderInput(
            inputId = "binary_power",
            label   = "Desired power",
            value   = 0.5,
            min     = 0.5,
            max     = 1,
            step = 0.05,
          ),
          radioButtons(
            inputId = "binary_test_type",
            label   = "Test direction:",
            choices = c(
              "Two-sided" = "two.sided",
              "One-sided (intervention less than control)" = "less",
              "One-sided (intervention greater than control)" = "greater"
            ),
            selected = "two.sided"
          ),
          radioButtons(
            inputId = "binary_effect_type",
            label   = "Specify the effect to detect as:",
            choices = c("Risk difference" = "rd", "Odds ratio" = "or"),
            selected = "rd"
          ),
          conditionalPanel(
            condition = "input.binary_effect_type == 'rd'",
            numericInput(
              inputId = "binary_rd_min",
              label   = "Minimum risk difference to detect",
              value   = 0.1,
              min     = -1,
              max     = 1,
              step = 0.05,
            ),
            numericInput(
              inputId = "binary_rd_max",
              label   = "Maximum risk difference to detect",
              value   = 0.1,
              min     = -1,
              max     = 1,
              step = 0.05,
            ),
            numericInput(
              inputId = "binary_rd_step",
              label   = "Step size",
              value   = 0.05,
              min     = 0.001,
              step = 0.05,
            )
          ),
          conditionalPanel(
            condition = "input.binary_effect_type == 'or'",
            numericInput(
              inputId = "binary_or_min",
              label   = "Minimum odds ratio to detect",
              value   = 0.1,
              min     = 0,
              step = 0.1,
            ),
            numericInput(
              inputId = "binary_or_max",
              label   = "Maximum odds ratio to detect",
              value   = 0.8,
              min     = 0,
              step = 0.1,
            ),
            numericInput(
              inputId = "binary_or_step",
              label   = "Step size",
              value   = 0.1,
              min     = 0.001,
              step = 0.1,
            )
          ),
          useWaiter(),
          hr(),
          h4("Simulation check"),
          p("The frequentist 'power' concept might be better understood by simulation, that is, we simulate trials under exact same conditions again and again. Click 'New simulation (new seed)' below to simulate trials for the scenario with the minimum odds ratio (or minimum risk difference) above and compare the empirical rejection rate to the target power. Plots 2 and 3 only appear once you have run a simulation, and are not updated automatically when the scenario or number of trials changes -- click the button again to re-run with the current settings."),
          uiOutput("sim_scenario_ui"),
          numericInput(
            inputId = "n_sim",
            label   = "Number of simulated trials",
            value   = 100,
            min     = 100,
            max     = 1000,
            step = 100,
          ),
          actionButton(
            inputId = "resim_binary",
            label   = "New simulation (new seed)"
          ),
          br(), br(),
          textOutput("seed_display_binary")

        ),
        mainPanel(
          tableOutput("table1"),
          # plotOutput("plot1"),
          plotOutput("plot_sim_hist"),
          conditionalPanel(
            condition = "input.resim_binary > 0",
            plotOutput("plot_sim"),
            plotOutput("plot_sim_ci")
          ),
          hr(),
          h4("Reproducible R output for minimal scenario"),
          verbatimTextOutput("power_prop_test_output")

        )
      )
    ),
    tabPanel(
      "Continuous outcome",
      br(),
      div(
        style = "border: 1px solid #ccc; border-radius: 5px; padding: 10px 15px; margin-bottom: 15px;",
        tags$strong("Case scenario 2: The ESCAPE trial reported the EuroQoL Group 5-Dimension Self-Report Questionnaire (EQ-5D) visual-analogue scale as secondary outcome. Let us assume you use the EQ-5D as primary outcome for a sample size calculation. The authors reported the medians and interquartile ranges of the EQ-5D. For pragmatic reasons let's assume that they reported a mean EQ-5D in the control group of 65 (80 in the intervention arm). In both groups an interquartile range of 30 was reported. The common standard deviation can be approximated by the reported interquartile ranges and is 31. The default values of the App are set to match the mean values and are set to a power of 0.8 and alpha of 0.05 (two-sided)."),
        tags$ul(
          tags$li("T8: Change the 'maximum mean difference to detect' to 5. How and why does the sample size change?"),
          tags$li("T9: Change the 'common standard deviation' to 15 and 60. What happens to the sample size?"),
          tags$li("T10: Plot 2/3 show the results of 100 repeated similar trials, that is, repeated always under the same conditions. Count the number of rejected trials and divide by 100. Then increase the number of simulated trials to 1,000. Count the number of rejected trials and divide by 1,000. What does this calculated number mean?"),
          tags$li("Continue with the tasks in the 'Ordinal outcome' tab above."),
          )
      ),
      sidebarLayout(
        sidebarPanel(
          numericInput(
            inputId = "cont_alpha",
            label   = "alpha:",
            value   = 0.05,
            min     = 0,
            max     = 1
          ),
          numericInput(
            inputId = "mean_0",
            label   = "Mean in control arm",
            value   = 65,
            step = 0.1,
          ),
          numericInput(
            inputId = "sd_cont",
            label   = "Common standard deviation",
            value   = 31,
            min     = 0,
            step = 0.1,
          ),
          sliderInput(
            inputId = "cont_power",
            label   = "Desired power",
            value   = 0.8,
            min     = 0.5,
            max     = 1,
            step = 0.05,
          ),
          radioButtons(
            inputId = "cont_test_type",
            label   = "Test direction:",
            choices = c(
              "Two-sided" = "two.sided",
              "One-sided (intervention less than control)" = "less",
              "One-sided (intervention greater than control)" = "greater"
            ),
            selected = "two.sided"
          ),
          radioButtons(
            inputId = "cont_effect_type",
            label   = "Specify the effect to detect as:",
            choices = c("Mean difference" = "diff", "Standardized effect size (Cohen's d)" = "d"),
            selected = "diff"
          ),
          conditionalPanel(
            condition = "input.cont_effect_type == 'diff'",
            numericInput(
              inputId = "cont_diff_min",
              label   = "Minimum mean difference to detect",
              value   = 15,
              step = 0.1,
            ),
            numericInput(
              inputId = "cont_diff_max",
              label   = "Maximum mean difference to detect",
              value   = 15,
              step = 0.1,
            ),
            numericInput(
              inputId = "cont_diff_step",
              label   = "Step size",
              value   = 5,
              min     = 0.001,
              step = 0.05,
            )
          ),
          conditionalPanel(
            condition = "input.cont_effect_type == 'd'",
            numericInput(
              inputId = "cont_d_min",
              label   = "Minimum Cohen's d to detect",
              value   = 0.2,
              step = 0.1,
            ),
            numericInput(
              inputId = "cont_d_max",
              label   = "Maximum Cohen's d to detect",
              value   = 0.8,
              step = 0.1,
            ),
            numericInput(
              inputId = "cont_d_step",
              label   = "Step size",
              value   = 0.1,
              min     = 0.001,
              step = 0.1,
            )
          ),
          useWaiter(),
          hr(),
          h4("Simulation check"),
          p("The frequentist 'power' concept might be better understood by simulation, that is, we simulate trials under exact same conditions again and again. Click 'New simulation (new seed)' below to simulate trials for the scenario with the minimum mean difference (or minimum Cohen's d) above and compare the empirical rejection rate to the target power. Plots 2 and 3 only appear once you have run a simulation, and are not updated automatically when the scenario or number of trials changes -- click the button again to re-run with the current settings."),
          uiOutput("sim_scenario_ui_cont"),
          numericInput(
            inputId = "n_sim_cont",
            label   = "Number of simulated trials",
            value   = 100,
            min     = 100,
            max     = 1000,
            step = 100,
          ),
          actionButton(
            inputId = "resim_cont",
            label   = "New simulation (new seed)"
          ),
          br(), br(),
          textOutput("seed_display_cont")
        ),
        mainPanel(
          tableOutput("table_cont"),
          plotOutput("plot_sim_hist_cont"),
          conditionalPanel(
            condition = "input.resim_cont > 0",
            plotOutput("plot_sim_cont"),
            plotOutput("plot_sim_ci_cont")
          ),
          hr(),
          h4("Reproducible R output"),
          verbatimTextOutput("power_t_test_output")

        )
      )
    ),
    tabPanel(
      "Ordinal outcome",
      br(),
      div(
        style = "border: 1px solid #ccc; border-radius: 5px; padding: 10px 15px; margin-bottom: 15px;",
        tags$strong("Case scenario 3: The ESCAPE trial reported the categories of the modified Rankin Score (mRS) at 90 days. The mRS is an ordinal outcome, that is, the levels of the mRS have a strict ordering. Let us assume we use the mRS as primary endpoint for a sample size calculation. For the control group the authors reported the distribution of mRS at 90 days of mRS0=0.07, mRS1=0.1, mRS2=0.12, mRS3=0.15, mRS4=0.24, mRS5=0.12, mRS6=0.20."),
        tags$ul(
          tags$li("T11: Use the noted odds ratio from task T2 as input in the 'minimum and maximum odds ratio to detect'. How many patients do you need? Why does it differ to the sample size from the binary outcome example?"),
        )
      ),
      sidebarLayout(
        sidebarPanel(
          textInput(
            inputId = "ord_p",
            label   = "Category probabilities in control group (comma-separated, must sum to 1)",
            value   = "0.07, 0.1, 0.12, 0.15, 0.24, 0.12, 0.20"
          ),
          radioButtons(
            inputId = "ord_test_type",
            label   = "Test type",
            choices = c(
              "Two-sided" = "two.sided",
              "One-sided" = "one.sided"
            ),
            selected = "two.sided"
          ),
          numericInput(
            inputId = "ord_alpha",
            label   = "alpha:",
            value   = 0.05,
            min     = 0,
            max     = 1
          ),
          sliderInput(
            inputId = "ord_power",
            label   = "Desired power",
            value   = 0.80,
            min     = 0.5,
            max     = 1,
            step = 0.05,
          ),
          numericInput(
            inputId = "or_min",
            label   = "Minimum odds ratio to detect",
            value   = 1.2,
            min     = 0,
            step = 0.1,
          ),
          numericInput(
            inputId = "or_max",
            label   = "Maximum odds ratio to detect",
            value   = 1.2,
            min     = 0,
            step = 0.1,
          ),
          numericInput(
            inputId = "or_step",
            label   = "Step size",
            value   = 0.1,
            min     = 0.05,
            step = 0.1,
          )
        ),
        mainPanel(
          tableOutput("table_ord"),
          plotOutput("plot_ord_props"),
          plotOutput("plot_ord_diff"),
          hr(),
          h4("Reproducible R output for minimal scenario"),
          verbatimTextOutput("posamsize_output")

        )
      )
    )
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {

   # Random seed used for the simulation check
   seed_binary <- reactiveVal(sample.int(1e6, 1))
   seed_cont <- reactiveVal(sample.int(1e6, 1))

   observeEvent(input$resim_binary, {
     seed_binary(sample.int(1e6, 1))
   })

   observeEvent(input$resim_cont, {
     seed_cont(sample.int(1e6, 1))
   })

   output$seed_display_binary <- renderText({
     paste0("Current seed: ", seed_binary())
   })

   output$seed_display_cont <- renderText({
     paste0("Current seed: ", seed_cont())
   })

   scenario_results <- reactive({

     if (input$binary_effect_type == "or") {

       validate(
         need(input$binary_or_max >= input$binary_or_min, "Maximum odds ratio must be >= minimum odds ratio."),
         need(input$binary_or_step > 0, "Step size must be positive.")
       )

       effect_seq <- seq(input$binary_or_min, input$binary_or_max, by = input$binary_or_step)

     } else {

       validate(
         need(input$binary_rd_max >= input$binary_rd_min, "Maximum risk difference must be >= minimum risk difference."),
         need(input$binary_rd_step > 0, "Step size must be positive.")
       )

       effect_seq <- seq(input$binary_rd_min, input$binary_rd_max, by = input$binary_rd_step)
     }

     results <- lapply(effect_seq, function(effect) {

       if (input$binary_effect_type == "or") {
         # Convert odds ratio to proportion in intervention arm, given the
         # control arm proportion
         p_1 <- effect * input$p_0 / (1 - input$p_0 + effect * input$p_0)
       } else {
         # Proportion in intervention arm directly from the risk difference
         p_1 <- input$p_0 + effect
       }

       validate(
         need(p_1 >= 0 && p_1 <= 1, "Risk difference implies a proportion outside [0, 1] in the intervention arm.")
       )

       # No effect (p_1 == p_0) implies no finite sample size
       n_per_arm <- if (isTRUE(all.equal(p_1, input$p_0))) {
         NA_real_
       } else {
         power.prop.test(
           p1 = p_1,
           p2 = input$p_0,
           sig.level = input$nominal_alpha,
           power = input$binary_power,
           # power.prop.test only distinguishes two.sided vs one.sided;
           # the sample size for a one-sided test does not depend on which
           # direction (less/greater) is hypothesized, only |p1 - p2|.
           alternative = if (input$binary_test_type == "two.sided") "two.sided" else "one.sided",
           strict = T
         )$n
       }

       data.frame(
         p_1 = p_1,
         p_0 = input$p_0,
         risk_diff = p_1 - input$p_0,
         odds_ratio = (p_1 / (1 - p_1)) / (input$p_0 / (1 - input$p_0)),
         # se_risk_diff = sqrt(p_1*(1-p_1)/ceiling(n_per_arm) + input$p_0*(1-input$p_0)/ceiling(n_per_arm)) ,
         n_per_arm = as.integer(ceiling(n_per_arm)),
         n_total = as.integer(2 * ceiling(n_per_arm))
       )
     })

     do.call(rbind, results)
   })

   output$table1 <- renderTable({

     df <- scenario_results()
     df
   }, digits = 2)

   output$plot1 <- renderPlot({

     results <- scenario_results()

     if (input$binary_effect_type == "or") {

       p <- ggplot(results, aes(x = odds_ratio, y = n_total, label = n_total)) +
         labs(
           x = "Odds ratio",
           title = "Required sample size across a range of odds ratios"
         ) +
         scale_x_log10(breaks = sort(unique(results$odds_ratio)))

     } else {

       p <- ggplot(results, aes(x = risk_diff, y = n_total, label = n_total)) +
         labs(
           x = "Risk difference",
           title = "Required sample size across a range of risk differences"
         ) +
         scale_x_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(results$risk_diff)))
     }

     p +
       geom_line() +
       geom_point() +
       labs(
         y = "Total sample size required",
         caption = paste0(
           "power = ", input$binary_power,
           ", control proportion = ", input$p_0,
           ", alpha = ", input$nominal_alpha
         )
       ) +
       geom_label() + theme_bw() + theme(panel.grid = element_blank())
   })

   # Scenarios with a required sample size
   sim_scenarios <- reactive({
     df <- scenario_results()
     df[!is.na(df$n_per_arm), , drop = FALSE]
   })

   # Scenarios with the minimum odds ratio (equivalently, minimum effect)
   min_or_scenario <- reactive({
     df <- sim_scenarios()

     validate(
       need(nrow(df) > 0, "No scenario above has a well-defined sample size to simulate (e.g. all involve a null effect).")
     )

     df[which.min(df$odds_ratio), , drop = FALSE]
   })

   output$power_prop_test_output <- renderPrint({

     row <- min_or_scenario()
     alternative <- if (input$binary_test_type == "two.sided") "two.sided" else "one.sided"

     cat(
       "power.prop.test(\n",
       "  p1 = ", round(row$p_1, 4), ",\n",
       "  p2 = ", round(row$p_0, 4), ",\n",
       "  sig.level = ", input$nominal_alpha, ",\n",
       "  power = ", input$binary_power, ",\n",
       "  alternative = \"", alternative, "\",\n",
       "  strict = TRUE\n",
       ")\n\n",
       sep = ""
     )

     print(power.prop.test(
       p1 = row$p_1,
       p2 = row$p_0,
       sig.level = input$nominal_alpha,
       power = input$binary_power,
       alternative = alternative,
       strict = TRUE
     ))
   })

   output$sim_scenario_ui <- renderUI({

     row <- min_or_scenario()

     mismatched <- (input$binary_test_type == "less" && row$p_1 > row$p_0) ||
       (input$binary_test_type == "greater" && row$p_1 < row$p_0)

     tagList(
       p(
         strong("Simulated scenario: "),
         paste0(
           "RD = ", round(row$risk_diff, 2),
           ", OR = ", round(row$odds_ratio, 2),
           ", n/arm = ", row$n_per_arm
         )
       ),
       if (mismatched) {
         p(
           style = "color: firebrick;",
           "Warning: this scenario's effect runs opposite to the selected one-sided hypothesis, so the test will rarely reject and empirical power will be near zero."
         )
       }
     )
   })

   # Simulation setup
   sim_params_binary <- reactive({

     row <- min_or_scenario()

     alpha <- input$nominal_alpha
     test_type <- input$binary_test_type
     tside <- if (test_type == "two.sided") 2 else 1

     # power.prop.test's sample size is derived from a Gaussian
     # approximation
     critical_limit <- qnorm(1 - alpha / tside)

     list(
       n_per_arm = row$n_per_arm,
       p_0 = row$p_0,
       p_1 = row$p_1,
       alpha = alpha,
       test_type = test_type,
       critical_limit = critical_limit
     )
   })

   simulation_results <- eventReactive(input$resim_binary, {

     req(input$n_sim)

     params <- sim_params_binary()

     n_per_arm <- params$n_per_arm
     p_0_sim <- params$p_0
     p_1_sim <- params$p_1
     alpha <- params$alpha
     n_sim <- input$n_sim
     test_type <- params$test_type
     critical_limit <- params$critical_limit

     # Re-seeded on every click of "New simulation
     set.seed(seed_binary())

     sim_list <- vector("list", n_sim)

     withProgress(message = "Running simulation...", value = 0, {
       for (i in seq_len(n_sim)) {

         # Ensure convergence!!
         repeat {
           x <- rbinom(n_per_arm, size = 1, prob = p_0_sim)
           y <- rbinom(n_per_arm, size = 1, prob = p_1_sim)

           p_hat_0 <- mean(x)
           p_hat_1 <- mean(y)
           p_pool <- (sum(x) + sum(y)) / (2 * n_per_arm)
           se_pool <- sqrt(p_pool * (1 - p_pool) * (2 / n_per_arm))
           z_stat <- (p_hat_1 - p_hat_0) / se_pool

           if (is.finite(z_stat)) break
         }

         est <- p_hat_1 - p_hat_0

         rejected <- switch(
           test_type,
           two.sided = abs(z_stat) > critical_limit,
           greater = z_stat > critical_limit,
           less = z_stat < -critical_limit
         )

         ci_lower <- est - critical_limit * se_pool
         ci_upper <- est + critical_limit * se_pool

         sim_list[[i]] <- data.frame(
           trial = i,
           prop_diff = est,
           ci_lower = ci_lower,
           ci_upper = ci_upper,
           stat = round(z_stat, 2),
           rejection = ifelse(rejected, 1, 0)
         )

         if (i %% max(1, n_sim %/% 20) == 0) incProgress(1 / 20)
       }
     })

     list(
       data = bind_rows(sim_list),
       critical_limit = critical_limit,
       n_per_arm = n_per_arm,
       p_0 = p_0_sim,
       p_1 = p_1_sim,
       alpha = alpha,
       test_type = test_type
     )
   }, ignoreInit = TRUE)

   output$plot_sim_ci <- renderPlot({

     res <- simulation_results()

     # Ordered by the interval bound nearer the null value 0
     order_col <- if (res$p_1 - res$p_0 >= 0) "ci_lower" else "ci_upper"
     # order_col <- "prop_diff"
     plot_data <- res$data |>
       mutate(order_key = .data[[order_col]]) |>
       arrange(order_key) |>
       mutate(trial_rank = row_number())

     n_rejected <- sum(plot_data$rejection == 1)
     n_not_rejected <- sum(plot_data$rejection == 0)

     is_two_sided <- res$test_type == "two.sided"
     ci_level <- if (is_two_sided) 1 - res$alpha else 1 - 2 * res$alpha
     ci_desc <- paste0(round(100 * ci_level), "% CI")

     ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = trial_rank, y = prop_diff, ymin = ci_lower, ymax = ci_upper, colour = factor(rejection))) +
       geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
       geom_hline(yintercept = res$p_1 - res$p_0, linetype = "dotted", color = "steelblue4") +
       geom_pointrange(size = 0.15, linewidth = 0.3) +
       scale_color_manual(
         values = c(`0` = "black", `1` = "firebrick"),
         labels = c(
           `0` = paste0("Not rejected (", n_not_rejected, ")"),
           `1` = paste0("Rejected (", n_rejected, ")")
         ),
         name = NULL
       ) +
       labs(
         x = "Simulated trial (ordered by lower or upper confidence interval)",
         y = "Effect",
         title = paste0("Plot 3: Point estimates and ", ci_desc, "s across ", input$n_sim, " repeated trials for minimal effect scenario"),
         caption = paste0(
           "Dashed line: null value (0). Dotted line: true risk difference (", round(res$p_1 - res$p_0, 3), ").\n",

     # Theoretical mu_alt: the standardized effect that gives exactly the
     # desired/target power (rather than the actual mu implied by the
     # scenario's p_1, p_0, n). The alternative distribution is shifted in
     # the direction implied by the selected alternative hypothesis
     # ("greater": positive, "less": negative); for a two-sided test
     # there's no hypothesized direction, so it's shown shifted towards

       res$test_type,

       less = -1,

         s <- sign(res$p_1 - res$p_0)
         if (s == 0) 1 else s
       }
     )
     mu_alt <- alt_direction * (critical_limit + qnorm(target_power))

     beta <- switch(
       res$test_type,
       greater = pnorm(critical_limit, mean = mu_alt),
       less = pnorm(-critical_limit, mean = mu_alt, lower.tail = FALSE),
       two.sided = pnorm(critical_limit, mean = mu_alt) - pnorm(-critical_limit, mean = mu_alt)

   scenario_results_cont <- reactive({

     if (input$cont_effect_type == "d") {

       validate(
         need(input$cont_d_max >= input$cont_d_min, "Maximum Cohen's d must be >= minimum Cohen's d."),
         need(input$cont_d_step > 0, "Step size must be positive.")
       )

       effect_seq <- seq(input$cont_d_min, input$cont_d_max, by = input$cont_d_step)

     } else {

       validate(
         need(input$cont_diff_max >= input$cont_diff_min, "Maximum mean difference must be >= minimum mean difference."),
         need(input$cont_diff_step > 0, "Step size must be positive.")
       )

       effect_seq <- seq(input$cont_diff_min, input$cont_diff_max, by = input$cont_diff_step)
     }

     alternative <- if (input$cont_test_type == "two.sided") "two.sided" else "one.sided"

     results <- lapply(effect_seq, function(effect) {

       diff <- if (input$cont_effect_type == "d") effect * input$sd_cont else effect

       # No effect implies no finite sample size
       n_per_arm <- if (isTRUE(all.equal(diff, 0))) {
         NA_real_
       } else {
         power.t.test(
           delta = diff,
           sd = input$sd_cont,
           sig.level = input$cont_alpha,
           power = input$cont_power,
           type = "two.sample",
           alternative = alternative,
           strict = TRUE
         )$n
       }

       data.frame(
         mean_0 = input$mean_0,
         mean_1 = input$mean_0 + diff,
         diff = diff,
         std_effectsize = diff / input$sd_cont,
         sd = input$sd_cont,
         n_per_arm = as.integer(ceiling(n_per_arm)),
         n_total = as.integer(2 * ceiling(n_per_arm))
       )
     })

     do.call(rbind, results)
   })

   # Simulations
   sim_params_cont <- reactive({

     row <- min_effect_scenario_cont()

     n_per_arm <- row$n_per_arm
     alpha <- input$cont_alpha
     test_type <- input$cont_test_type
     tside <- if (test_type == "two.sided") 2 else 1
     df_t <- 2 * (n_per_arm - 1)

     # power.t.test's sample size is derived from the t distribution with
     # 2*(n-1) degrees of freedom, so the matching critical value is the
     # corresponding t quantile (split across both tails for a two-sided
     # test).
     critical_limit <- qt(1 - alpha / tside, df = df_t)

     list(
       n_per_arm = n_per_arm,
       mean_0 = row$mean_0,
       mean_1 = row$mean_1,
       sd = input$sd_cont,
       alpha = alpha,
       test_type = test_type,
       df_t = df_t,
       critical_limit = critical_limit
     )
   })

   # Only (re-)runs the actual simulation when "New simulation"
   simulation_results_cont <- eventReactive(input$resim_cont, {

     req(input$n_sim_cont)

     params <- sim_params_cont()

     n_per_arm <- params$n_per_arm
     mean_0_sim <- params$mean_0
     mean_1_sim <- params$mean_1
     sd_sim <- params$sd
     alpha <- params$alpha
     n_sim <- input$n_sim_cont
     test_type <- params$test_type
     df_t <- params$df_t
     critical_limit <- params$critical_limit

     # Re-seeded on every click of "New simulation"
     set.seed(seed_cont())

     sim_list <- vector("list", n_sim)

     withProgress(message = "Running simulation...", value = 0, {
       for (i in seq_len(n_sim)) {

         # Convergence!!
         repeat {
           x <- rnorm(n_per_arm, mean = mean_0_sim, sd = sd_sim)
           y <- rnorm(n_per_arm, mean = mean_1_sim, sd = sd_sim)

           sp <- sqrt(((n_per_arm - 1) * var(x) + (n_per_arm - 1) * var(y)) / df_t)
           se_pool <- sp * sqrt(2 / n_per_arm)
           t_stat <- (mean(y) - mean(x)) / se_pool

           if (is.finite(t_stat)) break
         }

         rejected <- switch(
           test_type,
           two.sided = abs(t_stat) > critical_limit,
           greater = t_stat > critical_limit,
           less = t_stat < -critical_limit
         )

         est <- mean(y) - mean(x)

         ci_lower <- est - critical_limit * se_pool
         ci_upper <- est + critical_limit * se_pool

         sim_list[[i]] <- data.frame(
           trial = i,
           mean_diff = est,
           ci_lower = ci_lower,
           ci_upper = ci_upper,
           stat = round(t_stat, 2),
           rejection = ifelse(rejected, 1, 0)
         )

         if (i %% max(1, n_sim %/% 20) == 0) incProgress(1 / 20)
       }
     })

     list(
       data = bind_rows(sim_list),
       critical_limit = critical_limit,
       df_t = df_t,
       n_per_arm = n_per_arm,
       mean_0 = mean_0_sim,
       mean_1 = mean_1_sim,
       sd = sd_sim,
       alpha = alpha,
       test_type = test_type
     )
   }, ignoreInit = TRUE)

   })

   output$plot_sim_hist_cont <- renderPlot({

     res <- sim_params_cont()

     # Simplified textbook power diagram, drawn on the standardized
     # (t-statistic) scale. The alternative distribution is shifted by
     # the actual noncentrality parameter implied by the scenario's mean
     # difference, sd, and n (a noncentral t distribution)
     critical_limit <- res$critical_limit
     df_t <- res$df_t

     se_pool <- res$sd * sqrt(2 / res$n_per_arm)
     ncp <- (res$mean_1 - res$mean_0) / se_pool

     x_min <- min(-4, ncp - 4)
     x_max <- max(4, ncp + 4)
     x_seq <- seq(x_min, x_max, length.out = 500)

     curve_data <- bind_rows(
       data.frame(x = x_seq, distribution = "Null (H0)") |>
         mutate(density = dt(x, df = df_t)),
       data.frame(x = x_seq, distribution = "Alternative (min effect scenario)") |>
         mutate(density = dt(x, df = df_t, ncp = ncp))
     )

     alpha_region <- curve_data |>
       filter(
         distribution == "Null (H0)",
         switch(
           res$test_type,
           two.sided = x > critical_limit | x < -critical_limit,
           greater = x > critical_limit,
           less = x < -critical_limit
         )
       )
     beta_region <- curve_data |>
       filter(
         distribution == "Alternative (min effect scenario)",
         switch(
           res$test_type,
           two.sided = abs(x) < critical_limit,
           greater = x < critical_limit,
           less = x > -critical_limit
         )
       )

     p <- ggplot(curve_data, aes(x = x, y = density, colour = distribution)) +
       geom_area(
         data = beta_region, aes(x = x, y = density),
         fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.5, inherit.aes = FALSE
       ) +
       geom_area(
         data = alpha_region, aes(x = x, y = density, group = x > 0),
         fill = "firebrick", alpha = 0.6, inherit.aes = FALSE
       ) +
       geom_line(linewidth = 0.8)

     if (res$test_type %in% c("two.sided", "greater")) {
       p <- p +
         geom_vline(xintercept = critical_limit, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
         annotate(
           "text",
           x = critical_limit,
           y = Inf,
           label = "Critical value",
           hjust = -0.05,
           vjust = 1.5,
           color = "grey20",
           fontface = "bold",
           size = 4
         )
     }

     if (res$test_type %in% c("two.sided", "less")) {
       p <- p +
         geom_vline(xintercept = -critical_limit, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
         annotate(
           "text",
           x = -critical_limit,
           y = Inf,
           label = "Critical value",
           hjust = 1.05,
           vjust = 1.5,
           color = "grey20",
           fontface = "bold",
           size = 4
         )
     }

     x_breaks <- switch(
       res$test_type,
       two.sided = c(-critical_limit, 0, critical_limit),
       greater = c(0, critical_limit),
       less = c(-critical_limit, 0)
     )

     p +
       scale_x_continuous(breaks = x_breaks, labels = scales::number(x_breaks, accuracy = 0.01)) +
       scale_colour_manual(
         values = c("Null (H0)" = "black", "Alternative (min effect scenario)" = "steelblue4"),
         name = NULL
       ) +
       labs(
         x = "t test statistic",
         y = "Density",
         title = "Plot 1: Null and alternative distributions of the test statistic",
         caption = paste0(
           "n per arm = ", res$n_per_arm,
           ", mean0 = ", res$mean_0,
           ", mean1 = ", round(res$mean_1, 3),
           ", alpha (red, ", switch(res$test_type, two.sided = "two-sided", less = "one-sided, less", greater = "one-sided, greater"), ") = ", res$alpha
           )
       ) +
       theme_bw() + theme(panel.grid = element_blank())
   })

   # Experimental-arm category probabilities implied by a common odds
   # ratio applied to the control-arm probabilities (assumes proportional
   # odds).
   ord_pe_from_or <- function(pc, or) {
     cum_pe <- or * cumsum(pc) / (1 - cumsum(pc) + or * cumsum(pc))
     diff(c(0, cum_pe))
   }

   scenario_results_ord <- reactive({

     p_vec <- as.numeric(strsplit(input$ord_p, ",")[[1]])

     validate(
       need(!any(is.na(p_vec)), "Category probabilities must be a comma-separated list of numbers."),
       need(length(p_vec) >= 2, "Provide at least two category probabilities."),
       need(all(p_vec > 0), "Category probabilities must be positive."),
       need(abs(sum(p_vec) - 1) < 1e-6, "Category probabilities must sum to 1.")
     )

     category <- factor(seq_along(p_vec), levels = seq_along(p_vec))

     # Hmisc::posamsize() is inherently two-sided, so a one-sided test is
     # reproduced by doubling alpha, giving the same qnorm(1 - alpha)
     # critical value used internally for a genuinely one-sided test.
     onesided <- input$ord_test_type == "one.sided"
     alpha_hmisc <- if (onesided) 2 * input$ord_alpha else input$ord_alpha

     validate(
       need(input$or_max >= input$or_min, "Maximum odds ratio must be >= minimum odds ratio."),
       need(input$or_step > 0, "Step size must be positive.")
     )

     or_seq <- seq(input$or_min, input$or_max, by = input$or_step)

     fits <- lapply(or_seq, function(or) {

       pe_vec <- ord_pe_from_or(p_vec, or)
       pbar <- (p_vec + pe_vec) / 2

       res <- Hmisc::posamsize(
         p = pbar,
         odds.ratio = or,
         fraction = 0.5,
         alpha = alpha_hmisc,
         power = input$ord_power
       )

       n_total <- ceiling(res$n)

       list(
         nC = ceiling(n_total / 2),
         nE = ceiling(n_total / 2),
         n = n_total,
         probtable = data.frame(pc = p_vec, pe = pe_vec)
       )
     })

     summary_results <- Map(function(out, or) {
       data.frame(
         odds_ratio = or,
         n_control = out$nC,
         n_experimental = out$nE,
         n_total = out$n
       )
     }, fits, or_seq)

     prop_results <- Map(function(out, or) {
       pt <- out$probtable
       abs_diff <- abs(pt$pe - pt$pc)

       rbind(
         data.frame(odds_ratio = or, group = "Intervention", category = category, proportion = pt$pe),
         data.frame(odds_ratio = or, group = "Control", category = category, proportion = pt$pc),
         data.frame(odds_ratio = or, group = "Absolute difference", category = category, proportion = abs_diff)
       )
     }, fits, or_seq)

     list(
       summary = do.call(rbind, summary_results),
       proportions = do.call(rbind, prop_results),
       fits = fits
     )
   })

   output$table_ord <- renderTable({

     scenario_results_ord()$summary
   }, digits=3)

   # Scenario with the minimum odds ratio (equivalently, minimum effect
   # and largest required sample size)
   min_or_scenario_ord <- reactive({
     res <- scenario_results_ord()
     df <- res$summary

     validate(
       need(nrow(df) > 0, "No scenario above has a well-defined sample size.")
     )

     idx <- which.min(df$odds_ratio)
     list(row = df[idx, , drop = FALSE], fit = res$fits[[idx]])
   })

   output$posamsize_output <- renderPrint({

     sc <- min_or_scenario_ord()
     row <- sc$row

     p_vec <- as.numeric(strsplit(input$ord_p, ",")[[1]])
     onesided <- input$ord_test_type == "one.sided"

     # Hmisc::posamsize() expects the *pooled* (average, across arms)
     # per-category probability, and always treats alpha as two-sided --
     # a one-sided test is reproduced by doubling alpha, giving the same
     # qnorm(1 - alpha) critical value
     or_val <- row$odds_ratio
     alpha_hmisc <- if (onesided) 2 * input$ord_alpha else input$ord_alpha

     cat(
       "# Control group category probabilities\n",
       "pc <- c(", paste(round(p_vec, 4), collapse = ", "), ")\n\n",
       "# Experimental-arm probabilities implied by the odds ratio\n",
       "# (assumes proportional odds), and their average with the\n",
       "# control-arm probabilities\n",
       "pe <- ", or_val, " * cumsum(pc) / (1 - cumsum(pc) + ", or_val, " * cumsum(pc))\n",
       "pe <- diff(c(0, pe))\n",
       "pbar <- (pc + pe) / 2\n\n",
       "Hmisc::posamsize(\n",
       "  p = pbar,\n",
       "  odds.ratio = ", or_val, ",\n",
       "  fraction = 0.5,\n",
       "  alpha = ", alpha_hmisc, ",\n",
       "  power = ", input$ord_power, "\n",
       ")\n\n",
       sep = ""
     )

     pt <- sc$fit$probtable
     pbar <- (pt$pc + pt$pe) / 2
     print(Hmisc::posamsize(
       p = pbar,
       odds.ratio = or_val,
       fraction = 0.5,
       alpha = alpha_hmisc,
       power = input$ord_power
     ))
   })

   output$plot_ord <- renderPlot({

     ggplot(scenario_results_ord()$summary, aes(x = odds_ratio, y = n_total, label = n_total)) +
       geom_line() +
       geom_point() +
       labs(
         x = "Odds ratio to detect",
         y = "Total sample size required",
         title = "Required sample size across a range of odds ratios",
         caption = paste0(
           "power = ", input$ord_power,
           ", alpha = ", input$ord_alpha,
           " (", switch(input$ord_test_type, two.sided = "two-sided", one.sided = "one-sided"), ")"
         )
       ) +
       scale_x_log10(breaks = sort(unique(scenario_results_ord()$summary$odds_ratio))) +
       geom_label() + theme_bw() + theme(panel.grid = element_blank())
   })

   output$plot_ord_props <- renderPlot({

     prop_data <- scenario_results_ord()$proportions
     prop_data <- prop_data[prop_data$group != "Absolute difference", , drop = FALSE]
     prop_data$group <- factor(prop_data$group, levels = c("Intervention", "Control"))
     prop_data$or_label <- paste0("OR = ", sprintf("%.2f", prop_data$odds_ratio))
     n_cat <- nlevels(prop_data$category)
     # Category 1 sits at the top of the (reversed) stack, so give it the
     # lightest shade and darken progressively for later categories
     red_shades <- colorRampPalette(c("mistyrose", "firebrick"))(n_cat)

     # Cumulative boundaries between adjacent stacked segments
     group_levels <- levels(prop_data$group)
     half_width <- 0.9 / 2
     y_control <- match("Control", group_levels) - half_width
     y_intervention <- match("Intervention", group_levels) + half_width

     boundary_data <- prop_data |>
       arrange(or_label, group, category) |>
       group_by(or_label, group) |>
       mutate(cum_prop = cumsum(proportion), boundary_rank = as.integer(category)) |>
       ungroup() |>
       select(or_label, group, boundary_rank, cum_prop) |>
       bind_rows(
         prop_data |>
           distinct(or_label, group) |>
           mutate(boundary_rank = 0L, cum_prop = 0)
       ) |>
       pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = cum_prop) |>
       arrange(or_label, boundary_rank)

     ggplot(prop_data, aes(y = group, x = proportion, fill = category)) +
       geom_col(position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
       geom_segment(
         data = boundary_data,
         aes(x = Control, y = y_control, xend = Intervention, yend = y_intervention),
         inherit.aes = FALSE,
         linetype = "dashed",
         color = "grey40"
       ) +
       geom_text(
         aes(label = scales::percent(proportion, accuracy = 1)),
         position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5, reverse = TRUE),
         size = 3
       ) +
       scale_fill_manual(values = red_shades) +
       scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
       facet_wrap(~ or_label, ncol = 1) +
       labs(
         y = NULL,
         x = "Expected proportion",
         fill = "Category",
         title = "Anticipated category proportions by group across odds ratio scenarios"
       ) +
       theme_bw() + theme(panel.grid = element_blank())
   })

   output$plot_ord_diff <- renderPlot({

     # Separate plot (and y-axis scale) from plot_ord_props
     diff_data <- scenario_results_ord()$proportions
     diff_data <- diff_data[diff_data$group == "Absolute difference", , drop = FALSE]
     diff_data$or_label <- paste0("OR = ", sprintf("%.2f", diff_data$odds_ratio))
     
     n_cat <- nlevels(diff_data$category)
     blue_shades <- colorRampPalette(c("lightsteelblue1", "steelblue"))(n_cat)

     ggplot(diff_data, aes(y = group, x = proportion, fill = category)) +
       geom_col(position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
       geom_text(
         aes(label = scales::percent(proportion, accuracy = 1)),
         position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5, reverse = TRUE),
         size = 3
       ) +
       scale_fill_manual(values = blue_shades) +
       scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
       facet_wrap(~ or_label, ncol = 1) +
       labs(
         y = NULL,
         x = "Absolute difference in proportion",
         fill = "Category",
         title = "Absolute difference in category proportions (Intervention vs Control)"
       ) +
       theme_bw() + theme(panel.grid = element_blank())
   })

}
